steps.content: Crack.

The projection cuts out without warning.
When you turn, you see that the projector in Pixel's hand is already crumbling.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Whoops! So sorry, but the rest is premium content. Gotta pay to unlock.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: There's way juicier stuff ahead! Want to see how a total nobody pulls off the ultimate comeback? How she grows to power and declares war on the entire rotten academia all by herself? Want a front-row seat while she schemes and plots and drags those high-and-mighty types off their pedestals, one by one by one?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Then head over to the platform and smash that subscribe button! Officially launching next quarter, crowdfunding link in the description, and don't forget to like, comment, and share!

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: You... you...
Wittmann's lips tremble. He jabs a finger at Pixel and stammers:

steps.speaker: Wittmann
steps.content: You lunatic! You're insane! How are you still alive?! You... you're...

He tries to speak, reaching deep into his memory for that name. Yet the depths are crowded with too many students he has cast aside and forgotten, their faces worn away beyond recognition. Pixel cocks her head, and her pixel mouth twists into a mocking curve.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: What's wrong? Can't quite place the name? Yeah, that tracks. When you've gone through so many students, stepping stones, sacrificial lambs, tools you toss the second they've outlived their usefulness... how could one insignificant little me possibly stand out from the pile?

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: But that's okay! You know how it is at a grand royal ball. Nobody ever dares call the queen by name! Give it enough time, and people might forget what she was called, but they will never, ever forget what she did. Isn't that right?

Her screen lights up with an emoji crying with laughter. The girl skips about, all smiles, chattering without pause. So when she pulls out her gun and pulls the trigger, not a single person sees it coming.
"Bang!"

steps.speaker: Students
steps.content: AHHHH! She has a gun!
The lab fills with shrieks in an instant. You quickly stand between the students and Pixel while reaching out one hand to Pixel, desperate to halt her madness in its tracks.
You don't have to do this, Pixel! I'll make sure he answers for what he did, all of it. I swear. But if you pull that trigger right now, the case dies with him!

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Oh, Chief. You're really underestimating me.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Let's say I give you every benefit of the doubt. Let's say you really are different from the rest of them. One good person in this world, in this circle? That's not nearly enough. Not even close.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: He goes in, he pulls some strings, calls in a few favors, and walks right back out. You know it. I know it.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: You think I haven't once tried believing in justice? After all these years?
Pixel grows more and more frantic as she talks, her entire frame shaking. Her display flickers wildly in response, breaking apart into waves of distortion, glitch lines, and fractured pixels.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Enough! I said enough! I am done! Done with all of it! Ahh!

Possessed by frenzy, she pulls the trigger again and again, bullets tearing through the lab without aim. Reagent bottles explode under the onslaught, spewing corrosive fumes and burning liquid into the air.
The fire alarms shriek instantly, and the chaos spills out of the laboratory, consuming the entire research building.
Pixel, stop!
You chase after her, cutting hard around the corner of the corridor until she finally falls within the shackles' reach.
As you lift your hand, the shackles stretch silently toward the staggering figure with the computer head. Yet just before they can touch her, she lets out a startled cry and tumbles to the floor.

You throw yourself forward and grab her by the collar. Her head snaps up, and suddenly her computer head and that flashy patchwork coat disintegrate into a cloud of white pixels, scattering into nothing.
The figure now clutched in your hands is not Pixel at all, but the girl Wittmann used as a scapegoat in the lab. She huddles on the floor, pale as ash, her lips quivering.
You go still. Is this Pixel's power, or just an illusion? You glance back over your shoulder. The corridor behind you stands empty. No pursuers. Nothing but the fire alarm wailing on.
It's you... What's going on?!

The girl no longer struggles to escape. She raises her gaze, and in her eyes is not only fear but something indefinable, the expression of a person who has cut off every path of retreat and has nothing left to lose.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: Pixel got in touch with me before you arrested her.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: She said once you had a lead on those Mania materials, I'd be the one they threw under the bus the second you showed up. She said... why just sit there waiting to take the fall, when I could help her put on a little show and take that bastard down instead.
...Then how did you pull all that off? The computer head, the outfit, all of it?

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I don't know exactly. One second we were surrounded by all these white pixel blocks, just appearing out of nowhere, and the next... we'd switched. She told me to run this way. Said you'd follow me for sure.

Your grip loosens, and a short silence settles between you. What the girl describes reminds you of the projector you witnessed earlier. Pixel's ability, you realize, must be the power to print objects into existence from nothing.
During the chaos, she exchanged her conspicuous appearance with this girl. One body to lure you off, another to slip away. A remarkably clever tactic.

Your mind races. The anonymous informant who first flagged Professor Morris. Pixel, who surrendered herself so easily into your custody. The casual way she dropped clues about Wittmann's Mania research during interrogation.

Each moment was calibrated perfectly, each one steering you precisely where she wanted. The entire thing had been orchestrated from the start. She was fishing, and you were nothing more than the line she threw into the water.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I'm sorry for tricking you. If you need to arrest someone, just... arrest me.
The girl keeps her head down, her voice muffled. But you have no time to waste here, so you press her urgently:
Where did she go?
The girl gives a small shake of her head.

steps.speaker: Girl
steps.content: I don't know.

After getting the girl somewhere safe, you tear out of the campus. The wail of the fire alarms fades into the distance, overtaken by the chaos of Eastside: voices overlapping, horns blaring, the heavy thud of bass leaking from storefront speakers.
You stop in the middle of the pedestrian street and strain your shackles to their farthest reach, searching... The thread holds. She headed west. You break into a sprint.

One street bleeds into another as you push through the crowd, shouldering past strangers amid a chorus of curses and gasps. None of it matters. The connection from your shackles flickers, faint then strong, like a strand of spider silk trembling in a gale.

You burst into Eastside's most crowded intersection. It is Friday evening, and the city has snapped to life. People surge from subway tunnels, stream out of shopping malls, and trickle from every back alley until they merge into a single endless river of bodies.

Headlights, neon, and the glow of countless phone screens dissolve into one chaotic blur. So does the noise: laughter, chatter, footsteps, and the hoarse singing of a street performer under a distant bridge. You stand at the center of it all, nearly swept off your feet by the tide.
You stare at the faces flowing past you, every one painted with a different emotion, shifting and multiplying like the pixel expressions on Pixel's screen.
Then realization strikes. The connection from your shackles has not vanished. There are just too many of them—

From all sides, from everywhere at once, countless searing threads burst up through the ground and twist around your ankles, your wrists, your throat. Each one screams for attention, each one tugs toward a different destination. You fight to isolate a single thread, but the harder you struggle, the more tangled they become.
Dropping into a crouch, you sweep your hand across the chilly ceramic rim of a planter bed. Your fingers snag on a tiny, rigid object. You pluck it from the ground and hold it up to your eyes.

It is a scrap of plastic no bigger than a fingernail, warped and crude, its edges rough with the ridges of printed layers. Stamped upon it is a pixel smiley face with mismatched eyes and a grin stretching border to border. A whisper of Mania still lingers on its surface.
This is her power, her mark, her... taunt.
You straighten up and look around.

There, on a sticker plastered to a lamppost. On the handle of a public trash bin. Inside the basket of a bicycle left by the curb. Wedged into the cardboard sleeve of a milk tea cup held by a couple strolling past...

This Friday evening, along Eastside's most crowded street, Pixel's "presents" lie scattered around every unsuspecting soul. Strewn carelessly across every visible and hidden surface, each one burns with her unmistakable trace, each one hurls the same loud taunt:
"Catch me if you can!"

Your fist tightens around the plastic fragment, its sharp edge pressing into your palm. The crowd surges past like a relentless tide. You stand at the city's most clamorous crossroads, a solitary rock battered by the current.
Lost, you search the faces streaming by. Strangers. Ordinary faces. Faces with no ties to yours, forgotten the instant they pass.
Some smile. Some furrow their brows. Some hide behind headphones, expressionless. One by one, you study them, hunting desperately for something, anything, you recognize.
Then the truth settles over you. You were never going to find her.
Because at this moment, Pixel needs no elaborate trick. She simply has to remove the computer head from her shoulders and vanish into the crowd with a face no one has ever laid eyes on.

She could be any of them. The girl scrolling idly through her phone. The woman hurrying past with bags in both hands. The student kneeling to retie a shoelace. She might even be the stranger who just slipped by you, shoulder grazing your arm.
And you would never recognize her.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: I lost. I can't find you anymore.
The words leave your lips in a whisper, only to be devoured instantly by the roar of the city, leaving nothing behind.
In the days that follow, the Bureau presses on with its investigation into Pixel.
You had already glimpsed her past through that game demo, but records can be erased. A person who once walked this earth, however, cannot help but leave marks behind.
A faded attendance sheet pulled from the dust-choked archives. Shards of recollection coaxed from a retired professor's mind. A name crammed into the margins of an old paper's author list...

Slowly, painstakingly, as if piecing together a puzzle torn to scraps and scattered to the wind, you assemble the portrait of a girl named <color=#fb9259>Lucy</color>. And at last, you find her parents' address.
Old Residential District, Eastside Outskirts

They say this neighborhood was marked for demolition years ago. But the ones who live here are too poor to make a life anywhere else, even with a payout, so the plans gather dust and the people gather years, left behind as Eastside pushes on without them.

Grey plaster peels in cracked sheets. Cobblestones jut at odd angles. Roof tiles are split and seeping. Children in ill-fitting hand-me-downs race through the alleys, laughing, blowing tiny bubbles from jars of homemade soap water, and a row of parked bicycles clatters to the ground behind them.
You stand before a rust-flecked iron door, your hand hovering over the buzzer before you finally press it. Nothing. The bell is dead. You rap your knuckles against the metal instead.

The woman who opens the door carries the weight of decades she has not yet lived. Liver spots bloom across her skin, and her fingers are thick-knuckled, worn into that shape by cold water and detergent. Behind her, a man limps into view, a scar tracing a long, pale path from his wrist up into the dark of his sleeve.
Hello. I'm...

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Oh! You must be ${PlayerName}, the friend Lucy told us about! Come in, come in, don't just stand there!

steps.speaker: Man
steps.content: Sit, sit. I'll go get some fruit. Make yourself comfortable.

The man limps as he leads you in, his right leg dragging behind him as though it no longer answers to him. Then he and the woman squeeze into the cramped kitchen, his body leaning hard to one side with every step.

You let your gaze wander. The wallpaper is yellowed and peeling, and the walls carry the faint, stale scent of rain-soaked plaster that never fully dried. Curling, faded award certificates still cling to the living room wall. On the screen of the old television, a crooked handmade sticker reads, "A bright future ahead."
A chip mars one corner of the coffee table glass, and from it, a web of cracks spreads outward, stopping just short of a row of family portraits. In them, a girl grows up frame by frame.

A scrunched-up newborn cradled in loving arms. A child with pigtails, proudly holding a certificate between her parents. A young woman in a graduation gown, her arms draped over their shoulders, her eyes squeezed shut with joy.
The woman fills your cup with tea, then slides the plate of fruit a little closer.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Here, have some tea. Help yourself to the fruit.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: The road out here's not easy. It rained a couple days ago and almost washed part of it out. I told my husband, don't go messing around out there, but he wouldn't listen. Went and found some bricks, laid them down himself. Said he didn't want his girl stepping in puddles when she came home.
She says it like a reproach, yet a smile lingers in her eyes. The man drinks his tea in silence, offering no words, but the corner of his lips betrays the faintest movement.

steps.speaker: You
steps.content: Does she... come home often? For the holidays?

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: Oh, she's been so busy ever since she graduated. There's always something.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: We weren't well enough to make it to her graduation, either of us. So she mailed her diploma home so we could see it. And she gave us a bank card too, saying she wanted to send her salary back every month.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: We don't really know what she does at that research company, exactly. She's just... always working. I ask her if she's eaten and she never answers at mealtimes. Sometimes it's almost midnight, and her dad and I are missing her, so we try calling. But she's either still at work or already passed out. Getting her on a video call... it's been impossible.
The man beside her gives a nod. At the mention of his daughter, a tangled look crosses his face. Pride, certainly, but also longing and a tender worry.
He is a quiet father, the kind who speaks through silence. His fingers fidget with his teacup, his eyes wandering from the certificates on the wall to the family photo of the three of them.

Too busy with work. The project is at a crucial stage. The holiday is too short to justify the trip home... One hollow excuse after another, and yet somehow they were enough to sustain the image her parents clung to: a good daughter to be proud of.

What could you possibly tell them now?
That their girl is a wanted Sinner who just opened fire on someone?
That the child they have been so proud of their entire life was already crushed beyond recognition by a pitiless world, broken the moment they fell sick all those years ago?
In all this time, did even a whisper of what she endured ever reach their ears?
But the words refuse to leave your lips.

The dark spots blooming on the woman's skin. The long scar tracing the man's forearm. The tea still warm in its cup. The awards still hanging on the wall, faded and curling at the edges, too precious to ever take down. This family clings to the illusion of that good daughter. It has been the sole light guiding them through the long darkness.
They cannot survive another storm.

You open your mouth, but the words will not form. Instead, you lift the teacup and drink in silence. The liquid is bitter at first, yet as it slips down, the faintest hint of sweetness blooms at the back of your throat, so subtle you almost miss it.
When the time comes to go, the woman pulls open a drawer and retrieves an envelope, placing it gently in your hands.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: A few days ago, she told me a friend of hers would be coming by. Asked me to give this to you.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: If you see her... tell her to eat properly, will you? Real meals, not just whatever's quick. And to put on a coat when it's cold.

steps.speaker: Woman
steps.content: And tell her... come home when she has time. Come home when she's tired. That her mom and dad will always be here for her.
You promise her you will.
Only later, seated in the car as the city scrolls past the window, do you finally tear open the envelope.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Hey, my dear Chief! Thanks for checking on my folks!

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: I'm sorry I lied to you. I put on quite the show, and it was all to use you. I just wanted to feel like I'd gotten something back, some small revenge, some tiny repair, for a life that's already ruined. I wanted "Lucy" to finally get a piece of the justice she was owed.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: I've seen you working these past days, digging into "Lucy's" past, clearing charges that never should have stuck. I've seen all of it. Thank you. (That's right. I've been watching from the shadows this whole time! Here's your reward: one Pixel doodle sticker!)

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: I know someone like you will catch me eventually. So here's my deal: don't come after me just yet, alright? I still have so much left to do. I need to keep hiding in the dark, shining a light on the things no one else dares to say out loud.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Once I've dragged every last one of them out, once the system that let all this happen has been torn down, once the students underneath it all can stop being afraid, can chase what they want and get what they deserve... I'll come back on my own. I'll face whatever judgment you have for me.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: In the meantime, let me be your eyes. I'll go where you can't see and talk to people you can't reach yet. I'll walk through every dark corner for you until the sun falls where it was always supposed to, on every inch of ground the shadows have swallowed, and on every page that was always meant to be clean.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: (Oh, and I have a little gift for you! This list is real, I promise. Every name is tied to Mania research. So get moving and round them up, my dear Chief!)
A tiny chip is fastened to the bottom of the letter.

Now you see why Pixel spoke so pointedly about the importance of academic connections. Operating as a supplier and fixer in the underground, she has gained access to all of this with ease. And now, with solemn faith, she entrusts it to you.

You flip the letter over. On the back, one last line waits.
The paper around it is faintly wrinkled, as if a drop of water had once landed there and long since dried.

steps.speaker: Pixel
steps.content: Did she make you tea? Have some extra cups for me. My mom makes the best tea in the world.
Beyond the window, twilight settles over Eastside. One by one, the streetlamps awaken, weaving a slender chain of light that reaches toward a vanishing point far beyond sight.
You press your lips together gently. The faint sweetness of the tea still lingers in your mouth, as if a silent greeting had traveled across an impossible distance just to reach you.
Perhaps next time, she can be the one to go home and drink that tea herself.
